title: Runtime sync orientation playbook — Ivy journal
content:
Purpose: quick, repeatable agenda for the cross-cutting runtime + infra + console weekly. Orientation playbook for new attendees and a single place I use to capture action items and follow-ups.

Context / who should join:
- Owners: serving-runtime, infra, console ops.
- Optional: SRE on-call rotation, platform-engineering rep when we discuss infra changes.
- Attendee goal: leave with 1-2 clear follow-ups and one measurable status update (latency/error/throughput).

Pre-reads (1 hour prior):
- Brief metrics snapshot (Automated sheet link in #runtime-metrics; 5 bullets)
- Any blocking PRs in review (label: blocking-runtime-review)
- Feature rollouts scheduled in the next 72 hours (console > Rollouts tab)

Standing agenda (45 minutes total)
1) 0–5m: Quick lamp-up (one-liner and current blocker)
   - Each owner: 30s (name + last 24h action)
2) 5–15m: Top operational highlights (incidents, latency blips, quota hits)
   - Caller: on-call SRE or whoever observed anomaly
   - Data points to surface: p50/p95 serve time, error rate by model, queue length, KV cache hit rate
3) 15–25m: Deploys & rollouts (safety check, canary results)
   - Owner: release-engineering or feature owner
   - If canary failed: immediate rollback plan + owner for root cause
4) 25–35m: Console/observability gaps (dashboards, tracing, SLO alerts)
   - Triage triage items; pick 1 to action this sprint
5) 35–43m: Rotating deep dive (10–15m slot every meeting rotates across subteams)
   - This week: batching strategy hypothesis (Priya)
   - Next week: KV cache eviction policy (Diego)
6) 43–45m: Parking lot & close (confirm next sync owner and time)

How I capture action items (my convention):
- Short ID (AI-xxx) | Owner (mention) | 1-line task | Due (YYYY-MM-DD) | Acceptance criteria / notes
- I try to keep items <= 2 per person per week; escalate if >3 outstanding.

Live action items (working list)
- AI-001 | Priya Menon | Prototype latency-aware batch sizing config and run perf sweep on small Llama variant | Due 2026-03-10 | Results: table with p50/p95 and cost-per-token delta
- AI-002 | Diego Almeida | Investigate KV cache pressure seen 2026-03-01 (heap churn traces + JVM flags) | Due 2026-03-12 | Root cause hypothesis + small mitigations branch
- AI-003 | Samir Ahmed | Add a synthetic canary that runs through the console rollouts path and validates prefix cache preservation | Due 2026-03-09 | Canary runs nightly with success metric >= 99% for 48h
- AI-004 | Ivy Laurent | Draft a short runbook section: 'When a canary shows degraded p95 for >2 successive runs' | Due 2026-03-08 | Runbook text + PR to confluence

Notes to self / loose ideas (scratchpad)
- Consider adding a short "what to screenshot" checklist for meetings so postmortems have consistent artifacts (example: full p99 trace, request sample, canary config).
- Hypothesis: shifting some small models to int8 quantized builds reduces p95 variability during GC windows — try with 1 model as experiment.
- When we say "cache miss storm" we should standardize language: miss-storm vs cache-thrash. Use miss-storm in docs.

Meeting facilitation tips (short):
- If discussion drifts >5m on any topic, capture an offline action and move on.
- Assign a rotating scribe (I usually do it, but try to rotate every 2 weeks)
- Before closing: confirm due dates verbally for any new AI items

Follow-ups from last week (quick status)
- AI-087 (from last month) -- feature flag rollout cleanup (Rhea) — still in progress, small PRs merged; estimate finish 2026-03-14
- AI-091 -- SLO dashboard filter bug (fixed) — deployed 2026-03-04, monitoring 1 week OK

Parking lot (defer to ops retro or dedicated deep dive):
- Long-term: cost-model for batching vs model-compression across tenant types
- Console UX: add a compact mode for rapid incident scan (low priority)

Questions for leadership / things to flag in the weekly sync email:
- We need decision on temporary increase to dedicated capacity for EU region for one 48-hour stress test (cost estimate attached in linked artifacts).
- Request for 2 weeks notice for infra interrupts that affect rollout windows; want to codify in runbook.

End notes (meta):
- This doc is intentionally terse — meant to be a single-pane-of-glass for meeting prep and follow-ups.
- Archive older action items quarterly; maintain a short changelog at top if I perform structural edits.

Quick changelog:
- 2026-03-02: initial draft (Ivy)
- 2026-03-09: added live AIs and rotating deep-dive calendar
